name: Disorder with Multisystemic Involvement and Primary Lymphedema

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Multisystemic Primary Lymphedema

criteria.description: Presence of primary (congenital or early-onset) lymphedema affecting limbs
Evidence of involvement of at least two other organ systems (e.g., cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, dermatological)
Exclusion of secondary causes of lymphedema such as infection, malignancy, or trauma
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with lymphatic development (if available)
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as skin changes, recurrent infections, or vascular anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of primary lymphedema plus multisystem involvement with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis is clinical and exclusionary.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Primary congenital or early-onset lymphedema of lower limbs
pathognomonic.notes: Persistent swelling due to lymphatic dysfunction
searchTerms: swollen legs from lymph fluid buildup

pathognomonic.notes: Dilated lymphatic vessels visible on skin

common.notes: Frequent infections due to impaired lymphatic drainage
Progressive tissue changes secondary to lymphedema
searchTerms: chronic swollen limbs with tissue hardening
varicose veins or poor venous blood flow

occasional.notes: Accumulation of lymphatic fluid in body cavities
searchTerms: milky fluid buildup in chest or abdomen
lymphatic fluid accumulation in body cavities

occasional.notes: Structural heart defects in some cases

searchTerms: stiff joints and abnormal spine shape

laboratory: Elevated lymphocyte count in affected tissues
Normal routine blood tests excluding infection during quiescent phases
imaging: MRI demonstrating lymphatic vessel dilation and tissue edema
Ultrasound revealing soft tissue swelling without venous obstruction
genetic: Mutations in genes related to lymphangiogenesis (e.g., FLT4, FOXC2) in some cases
other: Histopathology showing dilated lymphatic vessels and dermal fibrosis
Exclusion of secondary causes by clinical and laboratory evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: Primary congenital lymphedema predominantly affecting lower limbs
Lymphedema with double row of eyelashes (distichiasis)
Predominantly lower limb involvement without widespread multisystem features

redFlags: Rapid progression of limb swelling with pain and erythema
Development of chylous effusions or respiratory distress
Signs of secondary infection or cellulitis requiring urgent treatment
references: Orphanet: Disorder with Multisystemic Involvement and Primary Lymphedema, ORPHA:568047
